quotes.text: Stripe provides an embed code composed of a `<script>` tag and a `<stripe-buy-button>` web component.
Invalid values are silently dropped, but your payment page continues to work as expected.
To join the Accounts v2 preview, go to [Account previews and features](https://dashboard.stripe.com/settings/previews) in your Dashboard and enable **Reusable payment methods for Global Payouts**.

You must provide the [client_secret](https://docs.stripe.com/api/customer_sessions/object.md#customer_session_object-client_secret) within 30 minutes. After providing the client secret, you have an additional 30 minutes until the `CustomerSession` expires.
For one-time payments, the Checkout Session uses a [guest customer](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/checkout/guest-customers.md) instead.

findings: This exact URL remains a guide to turning an existing or new Payment Link into a website buy button. Dashboard design choices produce embed code with a script and stripe-buy-button web component, and revoking the account's publishable key requires updating that embed (new raw:5-29; old raw:4-28). The new HTML example replaces the prior React example, but the prose still says React can mount the same component from a script in index.html (new raw:27,31-47; old raw:26,30-53). This is an example choice, not evidence React support ended.

The three attributes remain client-reference-id, customer-email, and customer-session-client-secret. Client reference IDs are up to 200 permitted characters and invalid values silently drop; customer-email prefills an uneditable address and invalid values also drop; the customer-session secret comes from a CustomerSession (new raw:49-55; old raw:55-61). Silent dropping is important because a working checkout does not prove the supplied identifier or email was retained.

Existing-customer reuse still requires server authentication, server creation of a CustomerSession for the correct customer-configured Account or Customer v1, and passing its client_secret to the component (new raw:67-93; old raw:73-115). The secret must be provided within 30 minutes and expires another 30 minutes later; generate a fresh secret per render rather than caching it. Those are session timing statements, not a guarantee of a completed Checkout Session.

The Accounts v2 note still distinguishes Connect general availability from public preview for other Stripe users, but the new capture replaces the old incomplete access-request fragment with a Dashboard preview setting named Reusable payment methods for Global Payouts (new raw:59-65; old raw:65-71; diff:71-83). Treat that as a documented preview enrollment path, not evidence of account-specific eligibility or a requirement for Customer v1.

CSP frame-src and script-src both require https://js.stripe.com when a policy is deployed; rendering requires a website domain, so local tests need an HTTP server (new raw:112-121; old raw:135-144). Without an existing customer, subscription or saved-method flow creates a Customer, while one-time payment uses a guest customer (new raw:129; old raw:152).

The diff is mostly sample-format and navigation change: hosted image URL, React-to-HTML examples, Node SDK-to-curl CustomerSession examples, a new Accounts v2 preview enrollment instruction, and heading whitespace (diff:1-179). It does not change the embed component, attribute limits, customer identity split, CustomerSession lifetime, CSP, or guest-versus-created-customer behavior. Other raw units in the shared summary were not compared for this job.
substantive_changes: The new guide supplies a concrete Dashboard setting for non-Connect users to join the Accounts v2 preview; the old guide has an incomplete access-request fragment (old raw:65-71; new raw:59-65).
historical_claims_to_preserve: Retain the 2026-04-20 buy-button raw as dated evidence for React embedding and Node CustomerSession examples; their absence from the November examples does not establish deprecation (old raw:30-53,73-109; new raw:25-27,67-89).

Retain the exact customer identity split: CustomerSession customer_account for a customer-configured Account versus customer for Customer v1, with server authentication and client_secret delivery (old raw:73-115; new raw:67-93).

Retain 30-minute secret-delivery and subsequent 30-minute expiry limits, non-caching guidance, CSP/domain limits, and one-time guest-customer versus subscription/saved-method customer creation (old raw:111-152; new raw:89-129).
